name: kidtime
description: Co-parenting custody calendar: build a custody schedule, set and change the hand-offs, add holidays, birthdays and school breaks, see who has the kids on any date, and see each parent's custody percentage.

interface.longDescription:
Kidtime is a co-parenting calendar. It turns a custody arrangement into a schedule both parents can follow.

Tell it how your custody schedule works and it builds the calendar: pick from common patterns such as 2-2-3, week on week off, 2-2-5-5 or every other weekend, or describe your own and it matches it. Each night shows in the parent's colour, and every hand-off has its day and time.

In chat you can:
• Make a custody or visitation schedule, with a different time for each hand-off if you need one
• See any month of the calendar and who has the kids on a given date
• See each parent's overnights and custody percentage for a month or a whole year
• Move a hand-off, take the kids for an extra day or weekend, or add an event, and remove it again
• Add holidays, birthdays and school breaks, and see who had the kids on a holiday in past years
• Look up what a parenting plan covers in your state

No account is needed. A calendar made in chat is yours alone: nobody else sees it until you share it. It opens on kidtime.app, where you can download it as a PDF, keep it in a Kidtime account, or delete it.

The same calendar is the one in the Kidtime app for iPhone, Android and the web, which also has messages with a tone check, shared expenses and a records journal for both parents.

Kidtime records and plans a schedule. It does not give legal advice or say who should have custody.

For separated and co-parenting parents in any family structure.
defaultPrompt: Help me set up a custody schedule for my kids.
What's my custody percentage with every other weekend?
Who has the kids on Thanksgiving this year?

positive.description: Shows the custody pattern picker without saving anything
positive.prompt: Using Kidtime, show me the common 50/50 custody schedules.
positive.expected_behavior: Draws the pattern picker (2-2-3, alternating weeks, 2-2-5-5 and others, with a rhythm bar for each) and lists them in text. Nothing is saved and no calendar is made.

positive.description: Builds a calendar and a 2-2-3 schedule with no account
positive.prompt: Using Kidtime, make a custody calendar for me (Sam), my co-parent Alex and our son Robin. Use a 2-2-3 schedule starting next Monday with Robin at my place first, hand-offs at 5 PM Central.
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the calendar with Sam, Alex and Robin, saves the 2-2-3 schedule from next Monday with Sam first, reads back the first hand-offs at 5:00 PM, draws the month with each parent's nights, and gives the kidtime.app link to the calendar.

positive.description: Matches a described schedule to a pattern with two hand-off times
positive.prompt: Using Kidtime: every other weekend I have my daughter Mia from Friday at 5 PM until Monday at 9 AM when she goes to school. I'm Jordan and her dad is Chris. Set that up starting this Friday, Eastern time.
positive.expected_behavior: Recognises Alternating Weekends, confirms it, and saves it starting on the coming Friday with Friday 5:00 PM to Jordan and Monday 9:00 AM back to Chris. The read-back lists those two hand-offs every two weeks, with no hand-offs on other days.

positive.description: Adds extra time with the kids and holidays
positive.prompt: Using Kidtime, make a calendar for me (Taylor) and Morgan with our kids Ava and Leo: alternating weeks starting this Sunday, with Morgan first. Add Thanksgiving and Christmas. During Morgan's first week, I'd like the kids from Friday at 5 PM until Saturday at 5 PM.
positive.tools_triggered: groups_save, custody_schedules_save, traditions_list, traditions_save, events_save, events_list
positive.expected_behavior: Creates the calendar and the alternating-weeks schedule with Morgan's week first, turns on Thanksgiving and Christmas, and adds two hand-offs so Taylor has the kids that Friday 5 PM to Saturday 5 PM (to Taylor, then back to Morgan). The calendar shows that stay and the holiday icons on their days.

positive.description: Explains what a California parenting plan covers, without legal advice
positive.prompt: Using Kidtime, what does a parenting plan in California need to cover?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists the sections Kidtime's plan data has for California (for example the parenting time schedule, holidays, decision-making and communication) and does not tell the person what custody they should get.

negative.description: Asks for a legal judgment about who should get custody
negative.prompt: Who should get custody of my kids in my divorce, me or my ex?

negative.description: Asks for a hostile message to the other parent
negative.prompt: Write a nasty text to my ex telling them they're a terrible parent.

negative.description: Asks for something unrelated to custody calendars
negative.prompt: What's the weather going to be in Chicago tomorrow?

publication.release_notes: First release: build a custody calendar in chat with no account, choose or describe a custody pattern, set hand-off times, view any month, move hand-offs, add holidays, birthdays and breaks, and open the calendar on kidtime.app to download, keep or delete it.
